status: TCP upload hardware tail drops and retransmissions reproduced with the old diagnostic endpoint and eliminated in the measured runs with the NI-owned GRO context. Firmware radio and hardware thresholds unchanged.
root_cause: The simulated TCP sink queued each NI receive packet into a second NAPI, adding a separate budget and GRO scheduling turn. Under burst load the CPU0-target EPP filled and L3TE VOQ admission dropped packets before the sink. Feed the same serialized NI NAPI GRO context directly, preserving flow order across poll CPU migration.

factory_authority.instruction: ca_ni_rx_napi calls napi_gro_receive at 0x1298, using its own poll NAPI argument

read_only_trace.limit: Sampling can perturb timing; the uninstrumented old endpoint return run separately reproduced 18 hardware drops and 18 retransmissions.

implementation: tools/live-pon-diag/pon_tcp_sink.c removes the second NAPI/FIFO and its backlog setting; uses the native NI owner NAPI; drains its GRO packets after endpoint detach before freeing the sink netdev. Hardware FE/NI path and packet checksums are preserved.
limits: RXQ RDU events remain visible and are not packet loss counts; they were not hidden or cleared.
The simulated endpoint excludes physical PON egress. The core radio firmware was not changed by this endpoint fix.
Throughput is still around 1.2 Gbps; removing packet loss does not establish maximum PHY-rate application throughput.
build: ARM64 final sink compiled from repository source with only the established test address changed from 198.18.0.1 to 198.18.255.1
unload_check: Final module unloaded successfully; management access and NI polling remained available.
